title: NIDCD says most babies recognize the basic sounds of their language by 6 months
summary: NIDCD says that by 6 months of age, most babies recognize the basic sounds of their native language.
body: The NIDCD speech and language milestone page says that as babies grow they sort out the speech sounds that compose the words of their language, and that by 6 months of age most babies recognize the basic sounds of their native language. The page also says children vary, even though they follow a progression. This most is NIDCD's wording. It is not the CDC 75-percent definition, and the page's checklist is credited to the American Speech-Language-Hearing Association. The page is a United States institute page from a 2010 publication.

sources.title: Speech and Language Developmental Milestones
sources.author: National Institute on Deafness and Other Communication Disorders
sources.note: US federal page, public domain. Opened 2026-11-26. The page prints NIH Publication No. 00-4781, September 2010, and no later review date. Supports the sentence that by 6 months of age, most babies recognize the basic sounds of their native language, and the sentence that children vary.
